tasks.title: design note: how red reads, credits, baselines and provisions a jest or vitest run
tasks.description: Before any code, write the design as a section of stamp-verification.py's module docstring; every implementation task below depends on it. It settles four things. (1) One runner-output module at layer 1, scripts/governance/_runner_output.py. It holds run-test-gate's summary and failure readers, moved and not copied, and red reads through it. It carries a per-case assertion flag that tells an expect failure apart from 'Test suite failed to run'. (2) Per-runner case identity and credit for jest and vitest: the FAIL <path> header plus the title chain. HEAD's case is the same chain with an identical body in HEAD's copy. Because ast is Python-only, choose between a text-level reading and a small stdlib tokenizer. (3) A per-runner baseline in which a new test file is absent rather than an empty stub. Settle it by first driving jest with and without --passWithNoTests on an empty suite, and vitest on an empty file (vitest was never driven), and record the results as dated history. (4) --deps-from <dir>, defaulting to --project, which links ignored dependency directories (node_modules at any depth, .venv) into the throwaway. Name the leaks a link opens: a workspace link into the shared tree, which is refused by name, and runner caches written back through the link. Also say how the project's .npmrc reaches the fresh HOME, or that it is named as dropped.

outcome.technical: The design for red-first under jest and vitest is written as a section at the end of stamp-verification.py's module docstring, headed as design not yet built; no behaviour changes. (1) One runner-output module, scripts/governance/_runner_output.py at layer 1, takes run-test-gate's summary and failure readers by move (each name checked to exist there; failing_suites stays because it reads the evidence layer) plus red's own tally and case readers; the two pytest summary patterns merge into their union; a per-case assertion flag is read from the runners' own shapes (jest's matcher hint or AssertionError under a bullet sets it, a thrown error or 'Test suite failed to run' does not; vitest's AssertionError under a FAIL chain sets it, 'Failed Suites' does not), and a crashed suite reads as a collection error, never red. (2) A case is its FAIL header path plus its title chain; a small stdlib tokenizer, failing closed, finds which test call sits inside which describe; run-time titles are refused credit by name; credit is refused when any HEAD test file holds the same chain with an identical body, matching the Python rule. (3) Driven on 2026-10-06 (node v22.22.3, jest 30.4.2 from an existing local install read-only, vitest 4.1.10 from this repo), recorded as dated history, measured once each: an empty test file fails both runners with or without --passWithNoTests, and a missing file exits 1 unless --passWithNoTests; so under jest and vitest a new test file is left absent from HEAD's run, while the empty stub stays the rule for Python runners. (4) --deps-from links ignored node_modules and .venv directories at any depth into the throwaway as real directories of per-entry symlinks, because vitest writes its results cache into node_modules; workspace links are refused by name; caches written back through a link are kept local or named as unwatched; git clean and rmtree must never follow a link, with a sentinel case owed; an untracked or user .npmrc is named as dropped and NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG is removed from the run. Of the session's red-helper findings, vitest without node_modules is addressed; the inline tools/ suite, the SIGTERM/SIGKILL cases red inside the throwaway and the stamp going stale on ledger creation are left to later tasks.
outcome.descriptive: The plan for making the red-first proof work for JavaScript test runners is written down, with both runners' actual behaviour measured first, so the tasks that build it share one design.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: the four questions the description names are settled in the docstring, both runners were driven and recorded as dated history, and no behaviour changed

Both documents carry one list sentence (house, pytest, unittest, jest, vitest), say the output decides rather than the command (a wrapper counts when the runner it wraps prints its own tally; any other runner is could-not-prove), and name runner_list_drift() as the check; neither restates the dependency-link sentences beside them. tools/prove-gates.py gains a red row (execute-task.md's list loses vitest, rl1 must fail) and an allow row (the list runs to the end of the text, an over-fire, rl3 must fail). Decisions: the name ends in _drift so prove-gates reaches it by suffix; only TALLY_READERS is graded (CASE_READERS agreement is not checked); the list ends at the sentence's full stop; the live case rl1 compares the AST reading with the imported table, two readings from two places.
Tests: test__refs rl1-rl5. Red-first: in the shared tree before the implementation (AttributeError, 222/223) and proved through the helper with --introduces runner_list_drift at HEAD 212470e8. Both prove-gates rows mutated in scratch copies: red row -> rl1 FAIL (308/309); allow row over-fire -> rl1-rl4 FAIL (305/309). prove-gates --selftest 37/37; test__refs 309/309, test__output 182/182, test__deps 299/299; ruff and vermin clean.
outcome.descriptive: The executor's instructions now say which test runners the red-first check can read, and a check fails the build if that list drifts from the table the check actually uses.

tasks.title: the orchestrator resolves the plugin root per spawn and again after an update
tasks.description: A brief resolved under an older copy was reused after the plugin updated, so its executors ran the old helper. Change execute-task.md's 'Resolve ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} yourself' line and orchestrator.md to say: resolve the root per spawn from the copy this session runs, and after a plugin update mid-run, re-resolve and say so in the run's output. Name /audit:doctor's running-copy check as where a session still on the old copy shows up. CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset in the Bash tool, so the literal variable is never what a subagent should receive.

outcome.technical: reference/execute-task.md and reference/orchestrator.md now tell the orchestrator and executor to resolve ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} per spawn from the copy the session is running, never to reuse a root resolved before a mid-run plugin update, to re-resolve and say which commands moved when the plugin updates during a run, and that /audit:doctor's running plugin row (_doctor_trail) is where a session still on the old copy shows. The orchestrator.md rule sits among the non-negotiable guardrails.
outcome.descriptive: The orchestrator and executor instructions now say to look up the plugin's location fresh for each spawned agent and again after an update, so a long run never keeps calling an old copy of the plugin.
